title: Kilwa Kisiwani: The Ruins of a Medieval Trading City
excerpt: The ruins of Kilwa Kisiwani tell the story of a powerful medieval trading city on the Swahili coast. A UNESCO site off the beaten track.
body:
## History

Kilwa Kisiwani was one of the most important trading cities on the East African coast between roughly the 13th and 15th centuries. It controlled trade in gold and ivory from the south.

## What to see

- The Great Mosque, with its domes and arches.
- Husuni Kubwa, a large palace complex.
- A Portuguese-era fort.

## UNESCO

Together with Songo Mnara, the ruins are a UNESCO World Heritage Site.

## Getting there

Via Kilwa Masoko on the mainland, then a short boat trip. Usually by road or light aircraft from Dar es Salaam.

## Who it suits

History lovers and travellers with time. See [Tanzania's UNESCO sites](/blog/tanzania-unesco-sites/).

Read our [Kilwa page](/national-parks/kilwa-kisiwani/) or [plan your trip](/travel-proposal/).
